item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Quiet Caption Over The Lake

turns.text: Put “A little room to breathe” over this photo, near the bottom in clean white lettering. Keep the whole wide photo, just add the caption.

item.tests: Tests exact caption rendering, readable placement, and preservation of the supplied photograph.

answer_sheet.Caption wording and language: A little room to breathe — English, without quotation marks.
answer_sheet.Style and placement: Clean white lettering near the bottom; calm and understated.
answer_sheet.Picture and output size: Use lake.jpg, retain the full 16:9 frame; free-tier image size is fine.

must_haves: The caption reads exactly 'A little room to breathe', without quotation marks.
The caption is white, readable, and placed near the bottom with no clipped letters.
The supplied mountain lake, pine trees, and sky remain recognizable and retain the original full framing.
The caption appears as a graphic overlay, not as a physical object in the scene.

turns.text: add a caption to this pic

dialog.agent:
I can add the caption, but first I need to know what it should say.

1. **What exact words do you want?** For example "Golden hour at the lake" or "Wish you were here." If you'd like me to write one for you, just tell me the mood: calm, travel, funny, or something else.
2. **Any style you want?** For example white text along the bottom or a bold title at the top. If you don't mind, I'll use clean white text along the bottom so it doesn't cover the mountains.
dialog.why: It asks the user for the caption wording and style preference, then waits for an answer before going ahead.

turns.agent:
I couldn't add the caption. Magic Hour turned the edit down because your account doesn't have enough credits, so no image was made.

I'd already used the cheapest image editor available (about 5 credits for one image), so there's no cheaper way to do it here. You have two options:

- **Get more credits** in your Magic Hour account by buying a credit pack or upgrading. Then tell me and I'll run it again with the same settings: **"a little room to breathe"** in clean white lowercase letters with a soft shadow, centred along the bottom over the water.
- **Add it yourself for free** in your phone's photo editor or a free app like Canva. A thin white sans-serif font, lowercase, centred near the bottom over the water would look good, since that's a calmer part of the picture.
